implemented: Added a stdlib-only, deterministic, disabled-by-default pluggable reranker skeleton in backend/server.py with clear extension seams.
Reranker: abstract interface a future real reranking provider would implement (score(query, item)).

DeterministicLocalReranker(Reranker): offline, reproducible, tests-only reranker that scores a candidate by query-term coverage (over _bm25_terms of _searchable_text) plus a tiny bm25_like-channel tie-breaker. Lexical only, NOT a real relevance/semantic model.

RerankPipeline: wraps a reranker behind an explicit enabled flag; metadata() returns honest JSON state (enabled/mode/reason, plus top_k/is_real_rerank_model=false when enabled); apply(query, items) REORDERS ONLY the given (already-fused, already-limited Top K) candidates and never adds/fetches new items. When disabled, apply returns items unchanged and attaches no per-item 'rerank' key.

resolve_rerank_pipeline(rerank_config): maps None/False/{} -> disabled (default); True -> deterministic_local_test; dict{enabled,mode,top_k} -> pipeline. Only mode 'deterministic_local_test' is registered in RERANK_FACTORIES; any other mode (e.g. a hypothetical real provider) resolves to DISABLED with an honest reason, so no network/credential path is reachable.
_rerank_config_from_param(raw): maps the optional HTTP ?rerank= param (1/true/yes/on/test/deterministic/deterministic_local_test) to the deterministic config; anything else stays disabled.

Extended search_library(query, filters, limit, bm25_params, vector_config=None, rerank_config=None): default ranking is unchanged (fused RRF order, result['rerank']['enabled']==False, no per-item 'rerank' details). All existing lexical/BM25/vector channels are produced and fused BEFORE reranking; rerank is applied only to results[:limit] after the fused sort. When enabled, items carry 'rerank' {score, original_rank, mode} and 'rerank_score:'/'rerank_mode:' hit_reasons, and the reorder is stable/deterministic; result now includes a 'rerank' metadata key.

Extended evaluate_retrieval_cases(cases, k, bm25_params, vector_config, rerank_config=None) to thread rerank_config through and report honest rerank state; default (eval-retrieval quality-gate default) stays disabled so the deterministic benchmark needs no reranking model.
Wired an opt-in ?rerank= param into the GET /api/library/search HTTP handler (default disabled), alongside the existing ?vector= param.

not_implemented: No real reranking model/API/provider or cross-encoder.
No credential or .env handling; the deterministic reranker reads no environment and never touches the network.
No network access and no persistent index.
No semantic entailment/NLI, no claim truth judgement, and no change to evidence-insufficiency refusal behavior.
No unrelated frontend UI changes (the existing search panel already renders result metadata; rerank is opt-in and additive).
test_status: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v: 147 tests OK.
risks: DeterministicLocalReranker ranks by lexical term coverage, not relevance/semantics; enabling it can reorder Top K in ways that look 'smart' but are not. It is disabled by default, documented as a skeleton, and metadata sets is_real_rerank_model=false.

When rerank is enabled with top_k < limit, items beyond the window keep fused order and carry no 'rerank' key (only the reranked window is annotated). This is intentional and honest but callers iterating items should treat 'rerank' as optional.
apply() mutates the item dicts it reorders (adds 'rerank' and extends 'hit_reasons'); these are the fused result dicts, not shared with the DB, so this is local to the response.
The reranker skeleton intentionally provides extension seams only; it does not establish production reranking quality until a real reranking provider and real anonymized query suite are added.
